summary: Mebeverine is a musculotropic antispasmodic used to relieve the abdominal pain, cramping and bowel-habit disturbance of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and related GI spasm. It acts directly on intestinal smooth muscle without the systemic anticholinergic effects of older antispasmodics. It is not FDA-approved in the US; this record is based on EMA/SmPC and BNF. Standard tablets are taken 135 mg three times daily, about 20 minutes before meals, or as a 200 mg modified-release capsule twice daily. It is generally well tolerated.
indications: Symptomatic relief of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) - abdominal pain, cramps, and altered bowel habit
Gastrointestinal smooth-muscle spasm and related conditions (e.g., functional GI disorders)

moa: Mebeverine is a direct (musculotropic) relaxant of gastrointestinal smooth muscle. It reduces spasm by acting on the muscle itself - influencing ion (sodium/calcium) flux and muscle contractility - without producing the atropine-like systemic anticholinergic effects, so it relieves intestinal spasm without affecting normal gut motility appreciably.

missed: Take the missed dose when remembered, unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume the usual schedule - do not take a double dose.
overdose: Overdose experience is limited; theoretically CNS excitability could occur. There is no specific antidote - treat symptomatically with supportive care and gastric lavage if a large amount was taken recently.
